背包乱斗拼好船，没有合成系统，同样的组件可以叠加升级提升数值，每局可以携带三个饰品做出特化构筑。把背包的精力系统改成了弹药、电力和燃料三种基本资源，每种资源的库存也能产生收益（弹药有投射物伤害加成，电力提高回避率，燃料有负面状态抗性），核心玩法就是不断的优化资源产出和舰船输出。10胜结束后可以进入不算分的无尽模式挑战各种对手，25胜左右就全是怪物船了，打不过可以抄抄作业再来一局。 demo玩了差不多20小时，正式版玩法更多了，除了传统的舰炮社保，还能搞出船员输出、自奶，不带武器的纯dot流派，可惜因为资源上限的设计，无尽50胜以上的套路全是苟王和无限宝石。 新版本改了金币获取，解锁价格全部降低，稍微打一下就可以全解锁了，新手推荐植物学家自奶充能、神射手社保、苟王刺客战未来。编辑界面按alt切换到舰船底板，shift预览界面滚动滚轮能预览更多升级效果。排行榜点连胜战绩可以看战斗记录。 8/10，推荐给喜欢斗蛐蛐的玩家。

对比测试版：解锁了9个本来就做好的船长和相关物品，有四个阵营依旧没做出来，取消了金币上限，然后就没了 问题：平局了是靠扔硬币来算输赢[但是每次都是对面赢]，意义不明的开局先后手也是扔硬币，很缺钱一回合就20块钱加钱道具就那么一个，也就是说能不能赢纯看运气能不能刷出来东西，然后每日任务是各个阵营单局10胜，也没有背包乱斗的加血机制，就五次容错，加上同归不算赢，想10胜真纯看脸，经典的老外不让玩家玩的爽的思想，测试版更新算是天天更新但是每次更不是修bug平衡调数值。就是大改物品机制数值，甚至直接删改饰品，不排除抢先体验也这样的可能 有问题的机制：辐射每有一层1s-2生命上限层数叠的很快而且扣的是上限，净化回来都没用，demo时是每层减百分百血量，非船员物品激活时每有一层入侵就有15%几率受到8点伤害，10层入侵就是80点伤害层数很好叠，而且你所有的非船员只要动都会触发这个伤害，而你不买最大生命值物品正常的血量是200~300，正常玩这么也有20多个物品，层数叠起来嘎巴一下就没了，全上净化物品才能顶过人家一个入侵物品，天天更新一直没改这个B入侵是不是不玩自己的游戏，但是你说他不玩吧又天天改，你要不入侵伤害数值给低点，要不就辐射净化完恢复血量上限 省流：星图依旧开发中，现在还是半成品2026/5/16，不建议购买

I want to say that I play a lot of games that are similar to this one, and this is what I think. The concept is nice. The audio and art are okay, nothing amazing. No hardware issues so far. The reason I don't recommend this game is that it does a really poor job of introducing you to the game. It is in early access, and you could argue that is okay. But how can you provide feedback if you miss the instruction manual on how to use it? There are a lot of things happening, and even after 10 hours, I am nowhere near close to understanding how things actually work. I get the general idea of resources for different weapons or the 20 different status effects, but that does not help me win the fights. I pick a character, start working around a specific resource or a few of them, and then 9 times out of 10, I lose to a build that looks way worse than mine, and I can't even tell why. There is a combat log, but either I have no idea how to read it, or most of it seems useless. The enemy weapon did 23 damage? How, when it says it does 7.5? Probably buffs, but then again, I am just guessing. My point is, it has things you would expect, but it needs a lot of work to be recommended. At least for me, when I started the game, it tossed me into a silver-ranked game and gave me a 100-game achievement without me even understanding what was happening, and I've never even played the demo. I feel like there is a big issue with the matchmaking of the game as well. But I think that is either because of a lack of player builds or the way all those types of games do the matchmaking, which feels wrong. What they normally do is match you with a board on the same day as you. However, they don't seem to care if that board has a broken build or not. Let's say you are on day 13 and you lost the first 3 matches, but then you lucked out on a unit or a build, so you won your next 10 matches flawlessly. So, when a guy who was winning here and there gets to day 13 and ends up facing your build, that guy is royally screwed. This is worse when people intentionally lose the early fights in order to get an economy set up. This normally means that you have less chance of winning the longer you play. Overall, it is a promising game, but it is not good enough to recommend.

Extremely frustrating at times. I don't know if this is the intended behavior or a glitch, but many of my runs get ruined because the items I need never spawn. Even when I intentionally acquire a bunch of rerolls to minimize the odds of getting screwed, I sometimes just get the exact same items over and over and over again in a way that is statistically impossible. Some components are more or less mandatory to progress into round 20+ (because they will improve essentially every possible build), and it feels incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to win the first 15 matches and then immediately lose 5 in a row (often within the first 10 seconds of a match) because I got railroaded into playing with only a weird, suboptimal subset of components. Random should be random. You might even make the "random" selections conform to player expectations by ensuring that items do not immediately show up in the shop again (even if a truly random selection would cause this to happen occasionally). I think there should be zero repeats of items until I have seen all of them within a given category at least once; this rewards players for using rerolls judiciously and minimizes how much effect luck has on the end-game. Edit* The item distribution is absurd. I went 30 rounds and saw literally 1 upgrade item so I could simply never upgrade my Thousand Year Drum. The upgrades are critical since they are the only way to improve unique items. They should drop at a predefined rate (e.g. every 3 rounds). Or at least give us a way to prune options we are never going to use so they don't show up constantly. Edit2* There is absolutely no meta game once you hit round 30 because the time to kill is literally <10 seconds in 99% of matches (and <2 seconds in about 20%). The game is incredibly unbalanced as some builds deal literally 10000 damage in the first 5 seconds. Unless you also build towards this, you will lose every single match as it is the only viable strategy. I deliberately took the tankiest captain, gave him the starting item that reduces damage by 50% for the first 7 seconds, acquired the max level freight engine (which offsets ~15 weight), and used all of that bonus weight to buy things that would increase my survivability. Didn't matter. I spent hours on this ship and went undefeated to level 30; at this point, I immediately lost 5 of the next 6 matches before my own items could even activate (and I had 30 speed and ~50% charge time reductions on most of my important items as well). There is simply no other strategy that works beyond dealing catastrophic damage in the opening 5 seconds. Weapons need a universal nerf in DPS so there is an incentive to take more of them rather than supercharge one high level item, there should be caps on how many effects can be present on a single weapon simultaneously, the weight system is too low and too punishing (taking an additional weight slows all of your items by 3% while adding a measly 25 health points in ship tiles). It is also tedious to never add new tiles to your ship for 20+ rounds. I want a hard counter against burst damage so other builds are viable at rounds>30; make the bulwark item literally -90% damage for the first 10 seconds (applying the effect to both players would maybe help balance this). This would effectively punish players who build ships with 0 survivability and 0 sustain since those only start to matter when the match lasts >5 seconds.

[h1]与舰同沉：站至最后一刻，自刎归天[/h1] 很好玩的一款背包管理加自走棋类的游戏，游戏的画风偏向硬核的机器，重型机器，激光射击等的感觉，而且游戏整体是天空题材，我们所管理的是一艘飞船 游戏采用的是这类游戏一贯的异步pvp，我们会匹配到其他玩家以前的游玩数据，（不过我还没碰见过自己，不知道一直失败会不会碰见自己），而且似乎是根据段位来匹配数据 为了丰富游戏玩法，游戏做了些任务系统来让游戏不那么乏味，奖励的金币则是用来兑换初始角色，每个角色有不同的被动，或者与其他道具，武器等的连携效果，以及初始飞船的情况也不同 与正常的背包管理相同的一点，我们需要在战斗结束后进入商店购物，买飞船的其他部分组件，武器，甚至是船员 游戏中道具分了不同的阵容所属，以提供相应的属性，而根据部分武器，船员等等的被动来进行连携效果，游戏提供了三种基础资源，不同武器等等会消耗不同资源造成伤害，而伤害类型与各种加成也有相当多独特的计算方式 游戏在在武器方面下了很多心思，我们不仅仅是需要在一定的格子中防止武器，部分武器第一格需要在格子以外，而武器的多种品阶也是需要注意的一点 至于船员，也都设置了特殊效果，游戏中只要是两个相同道具就可以升级，而不是需要两个同等级的道具，这点做的挺好的，游玩过程中的养成部分加快了，让游戏节奏变快了 游戏战斗过程显得稍微有点杂乱，基本都是蓄力足够就攻击，双方数值对拼，看谁先把对方血量降低到零以下，而我们最多可以失败五次 总的来说游戏还是非常好玩的，随机性靠商店，但游戏给的格子种类，武器种类等等相当多，喜欢这类游戏的玩家很推荐尝试一下 [quote]关注&加入∶[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45540934/admin/reviews_manage/]深澜探索者[/url][/quote]

A year ago this game seemed like a great idea, a fun and quirky Asym PvP game, now the more I play it the more it dawns on me just how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad this game actually is. You want to win consistently? Screw smart design, just gun cram till you're at zero ammo all the time. Want to reach the late game? Play the Ravaged Dredgemen and just status spam forever. The game doesn't actually reward smart gameplay, or intelligent design, trying to stay ammo positive will more often than not get you killed, instead just Alpha Slave or Status Slave yourself to win. I truly would like to see this game get better or else I'd just write it off without a review, but as it currently stands it is just soul sucking.

I want to start off by saying I do enjoy the game, but its flaws keep me from giving it a good review. My main issue with it is battles are far too short, especially early on where ships die in one or two shots with the right settup. Later in the game defensive stacking particularly health and armor builds become overwhelmingly dominant instead. Commanders like Ravva feel blatantly overpowered, and the balance overall feels extremely poor. Later on the matches can last a bit longer but getting there feels way too fast and would love to see a more drawn out battle. Considering the game spent a long time in testing before release, the state of balance is honestly surprising. I think matches need to last significantly longer for the gameplay to feel strategic rather than decided almost instantly. I enjoy the game enough to continue playing but I really am wishing some major system changes. There's simply not enough ways to play and If this game had item combines to make new items rather than just leveling them up it would feel a lot more in depth. Id much rather just go play backpack battles after a couple runs of this game as it stands.

DISCLAIMER: This is easily the best autobattler on the market both visually and mechanically. If you like this genre, this is way better than backpack battlers or similar clones. THAT BEING SAID, it suffers from an extremely severe flaw common to all autobattlers: A meta that eventually, inevitably dissolves into pure luck. Like the entire inventory management genre, it becomes insufferable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to play when you get out of that early having fun and exploring stage and into the competitive, "meta" stage of its ranked combat. Because the fundamental game loop is based off drawing certain items, if you don't draw them, you just lose. You can play smarter than early game players who don't know what they're doing. But when you get to higher ranks where everybody knows what to look for, it's mostly luck to get the stuff your build needs. At the same ranking level of top 50 global, I've both easily gotten to round 40 (35+ wins on a ten wins format) and lost with zero wins. Sometimes you just get zero good weapons, weapons boosters, or reroll components, sometimes you get 40 and effortlessly dominate everyone, until you eventually run into someone in deep endless with even better RNG than you. That's all there is to it.

It's all about the building of your ship. And I love it! After update: With the addition of Hoverboards as a universal item, I can not recommend the game. I understand that they'd like to expand the ability that is exclusive to one character to all, but this is the wrong way to do it. And having random crew members preforming their rolls better outside the ship on a Hoverboard is just too stupid for me to enjoy the game.

I want to like this game, I really do. It starts out interesting while you are working out the mechanics. Then when you've worked out the mechanics, you realise: 1> It's stupidly easy to get to the 10th win (which is where ranking ends) 2> Game is stupidly imbalanced. A large part of this is due to the fact you can stack lvl 1 items 3> A few items are pretty much essential after battle 20+ like "Diesel Power" 4> Basically how your run goes is more based on the luck of what pops up on the market than anything you do, assuming basic competency. 5> After around battle 25ish, almost all the builds you face are '1 shot kill builds' based around point 2, with like 5 Weapons computers + multiple fuel pumps + True shots to deliver one massive shot right at the start of the battle. This could be a really fun little game but it just starts falling over hard once you hit 20-30 hour mark.

"Meh" is currently how I feel about this game. It's early access so I'm sure things can and will change. Some of my biggest complaints/concerns: - No real item combos. You can upgrade every item with dupes but there doesn't seem to be any form of combining items? For example combining a projectile gun and a lightning item to make a lightning infused projectile weapon. - Match making seems to specifically hunt for things that will kill you when on a good build/run. I frequently go 7-0 and then get utterly destroyed several times in a row. - No real changing or fixing a build once you get going. Because of how the upgrade system works, swapping out a level 5 gun for a level 1 that you would rather have means you'll be losing a LOT of damage most likely. - Unlocks / progression doesn't feel very good. In other similar games you would unlock new parts that make future runs more interesting. This game doesn't seem to have much of that? Unless I'm missing it? All you seem to get are 3 passive slots to equip some basic bonus items into.
